clue.text: Proverbial way to conquer an arithmetical problem

definitions.meaning: the saying '... and rule' or '... and conquer' names splitting enemies as the route to victory
a sum in which one number is split by another, like 12 by 3

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle is offered as the famous recipe for conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says split your foes to beat them, and in arithmetic splitting one number by another is a basic operation.

clue.text: Chase articulated vehicle

indicators.note: spoken out clearly, so the word is said rather than read

parts.note: the word pursue, said out loud

explanation.surface: A pursuit after a long, jointed lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulated' looks like it describes a jointed lorry, but it means pronounced: CHAISE can be said like 'chase'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light horse-drawn carriage is an old kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Flotilla displaying the sangfroid of the senior service

parts.note: the Royal Navy is called the Senior Service in Britain, so its adjective is naval
coolness under pressure, emotional aloofness

explanation.surface: Ships at sea show the famous cool of the Royal Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse order: 'the sangfroid of the senior service' puts the navy's word first. The Senior Service is the Royal Navy, the oldest British armed service.
explanation.definitionFit: A small group of warships sent off on a task is a flotilla, a portion split from the fleet.

clue.text: Plain silver-topped tableware with gold underneath

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: plate is tableware, often silver-coated
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Simple silver dinner service with gilt underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for the tableware but is the noun: a flat upland.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableland is a raised flat expanse of land, a high plain.

clue.text: Note if consulate provides professional remuneration

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are worked up to supply something new

explanation.surface: A diplomatic office supplies a memo about payment.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator 'provides' is a loose one; all fifteen letters of NOTE IF CONSULATE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge made by a lawyer or doctor for advice is a payment to a professional.

clue.text: Like a hymn which has been amended and put back

definitions.text: Like a hymn which has been amended

definitions.meaning: turned the other way round or set back

explanation.surface: A rewritten hymn returned to its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-versed means given fresh lines of poetry; the ordinary word means turned around or undone.

clue.text: Buck about to make his name as a couturier

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a buck is a male deer
to sign is to write your name

explanation.surface: A young dandy is set to become famous in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' looks like a dashing young man about to make a name in fashion, but it is the animal; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturier is a fashion creator, someone who draws up clothes.

clue.text: A bumper cocktail, may be faced by…

definitions.meaning: in cricket a bumper is a short delivery rearing up near the batsman's head
a long mixed drink of spirits with soda or ginger ale

explanation.surface: A brimming glass of a mixed drink, which may be confronted by the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into the next one. A bumper is also a brimming glass, which feeds the drinks reading; in cricket, a bumper is a fast short-pitched delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bouncer rises steeply toward the batter, and the long whisky-and-soda drink shares the name.

clue.text: … a corkscrew?

parts.note: read with the previous clue: a cricket bumper is faced by the batter who starts the innings, and a bottle by the tool that uncorks it

explanation.walkthrough: Linked with 8 across: the first batsman in cricket faces bumpers, and a corkscrew is a bottle tool, so both senses share one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is a tool for unsealing bottles, and a first-wicket batter shares the name.

clue.text: Scotsman's own article written about one

indicators.note: the first piece is set down around the second

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Scot's own newspaper piece about himself.
explanation.walkthrough: AIN is Scots for own.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots speech uses this word for one's own possession.

clue.text: Security service fired worker for being extremeleftist

parts.note: MI, Military Intelligence, as in MI5
lit means set burning
a worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: Intelligence agency sacks an employee for radical politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like sacked, but it means set alight. The definition is 'extreme leftist', printed run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical activist of the far left is the classic aggressive campaigner.

clue.text: Substitute for underwear

definitions.meaning: to deputise for someone, to take over
a woman's undergarment pulled on by stepping into it

explanation.surface: A replacement for one's undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to come in for someone; a slip-on undergarment you put your feet through has the same name.

clue.text: Envy saddens — lies confound — and the other five are just as wicked!

definitions.text: Envy saddens — lies confound — and the other five are just as wicked!

indicators.note: to confound is to throw into confusion, so the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A moral lament that envy and lies bring sorrow, and five other vices are no better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confound' looks like a curse on lies, but it jumbles ENVY SADDENS LIES. Envy is itself one of the seven, which gives the whole clue its sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the traditional mortal vices of Christian teaching, alongside pride, greed, lust, gluttony, wrath and sloth.

clue.text: Energy from voltage over one thousand

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: V is the symbol for voltage
I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Power from a high-voltage source.
explanation.definitionFit: Vim is vigour or liveliness.

clue.text: 51 thousand domestic animals are just hangers-on

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
pets are household animals

explanation.surface: A huge number of household animals are freeloaders.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: these shellfish cling to rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: These shellfish clamp themselves to rocks, so they cling on, and the word is used for clinging followers.

clue.text: Provoke disturbing trait in anger

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for anger

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: disturbing means upsetting the order, so the letters are stirred

explanation.surface: An upsetting habit stirs up rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'disturbing' as an adjective for the trait; it is the anagram signal, and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy or vex someone is to rouse them, to needle them.

clue.text: Ego Peter developed with the woman he promoted

indicators.note: worked up into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peter's self-regard grew along with his favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: The feminine form ends in a double E, for a female favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A female protégé is a woman whose career is backed by a patron.

clue.text: Shipping line artist had a lot of chest trouble

definitions.text: had a lot of chest trouble

parts.note: P&O is a British shipping company, Peninsular and Oriental
RA, Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter on a cruise company's ship suffers from chest complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest trouble' suggests a medical complaint, but it is the box which, in Greek myth, released all the world's evils when opened.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this first woman opened a forbidden box and loosed every evil into the world.

clue.text: First unit

explanation.surface: The leading squad.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest whole number heads a count, and a single thing is a unit.

clue.text: I and friend take it in to copy

indicators.note: with 'in', takes the next word inside
with 'take', the friend's word holds the other piece

parts.note: a mate is a friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two friends accept something in order to copy it.
explanation.walkthrough: The container signal is split: 'take' and 'in' sit either side of the inserted word.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic someone is to copy them.

clue.text: Undertaking by monastic head is excuse for declining invitation

definitions.meaning: a promise made by a prior, the deputy head of a monastery
an earlier engagement given as a polite reason to refuse

explanation.surface: An abbot's promise doubles as a social brush-off.
explanation.definitionFit: An earlier engagement is the stock polite reason to decline, and humorously a pledge by a prior.

clue.text: This Finn could knock out a mouse

definitions.meaning: a ... Finn is a drugged drink that knocks the drinker out

explanation.surface: A Finnish man could floor a mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang names a spiked drink after this first name, and Disney's cartoon mouse bears it too.

clue.text: Idea a physicist gets of an uncharged particle

parts.note: a particle without charge is plainly not charged, giving the negation
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A scientist's view of a neutral particle.
explanation.walkthrough: An ion carries a charge, so an uncharged particle is NOT (an) ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a thought or concept.

clue.text: Master assigned pupils to it according to ability

definitions.text: Master assigned pupils to it according to ability

indicators.note: the letters are allotted new places

explanation.surface: A teacher puts pupils into sets based on ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assigned' rearranges MASTER, and the whole clue describes school streaming.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a class grouping by ability is called a set or band.

clue.text: After 10,a London money centre needs dogged commitment

indicators.note: the clue says that following ten come the remaining pieces, so ten leads the answer

parts.note: ten
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: After ten o'clock, the financial district demands hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the Square Mile, London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is persistence, stubborn determination.

clue.text: Peron in the Levant

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the next word

explanation.surface: An Argentine first lady in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Eva Perón was the wife of Argentine president Juan Perón.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva Perón, Evita, was Argentina's famous first lady.

clue.text: Scattered street Wren rebuilt

indicators.note: built again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A London street that Christopher Wren redesigned is in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Christopher Wren rebuilt much of London after the 1666 fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means spread untidily about.

clue.text: A consoling reassurance that one has reached journey's end

definitions.text: that one has reached journey's end
definitions.meaning: said on arrival: we have arrived at this point

explanation.surface: Comfort for a traveller at the end of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase soothes the upset and also announces arrival at a destination.
